target: Arkadaşım bize yardım edeceğini bildirdi.
english: My friend informed us that he would help us.
tip: To report what someone would do, the verb becomes a noun: 'edeceğini' means that he would do, the thing 'bildirdi' (informed) reports.

target: Güneş doğudan doğar, batıdan batar.
english: The sun rises in the east, sets in the west.
tip: The -ar ending normally states timeless facts: 'doğar' (rises) and 'batar' (sets) tell what the sun always does.

target: Keşke tatile gidebilsek, çok yorulduk.
english: I wish we could go on vacation–we're so tired.
tip: 'keşke' means if only and pairs with a verb in -se: 'keşke ... gidebilsek' means I wish we could go.

target: Sabahları çay içmeden güne başlayamam.
english: I can't start the day without drinking tea in the mornings.
tip: The -meden ending means without doing: 'çay içmeden' means without drinking tea.

target: Yaz gelince günler uzar, geceler kısalır.
english: When summer comes days lengthen, nights shorten.
tip: Adding -ince to a verb means when or as soon as: 'yaz gelince' means when summer comes.

target: Yarın serbest misiniz, birlikte gezebilir miyiz?
english: Are you free tomorrow, could we explore together?
tip: -ebilir added to a verb means can or could: 'gez' plus -ebilir gives 'gezebilir', so 'gezebilir miyiz' asks could we wander.

target: Hızlıca giyinip evden çıktım, otobüsü kaçırmamak için.
english: I quickly got dressed and left the house to not miss the bus.
tip: The -ip ending links two verbs done by one person: 'giyinip evden çıktım' means got dressed and left the house, only the last verb fully conjugated.

target: Eskiden burada bir orman varmış, şimdi bina yapılmış.
english: There used to be a forest here apparently, but now buildings have been built.
tip: The -mış ending marks something heard or inferred, not witnessed: 'varmış' means there apparently was, and 'yapılmış', apparently built.

target: Ankara'da tıp okudu.
english: He studied medicine in Ankara.
tip: Proper names take an apostrophe before case endings: 'Ankara'da' means in Ankara, the -da part meaning in or at.

target: Komşudan şeker istedim.
english: I asked the neighbor for sugar.
tip: To ask someone for something, put -dan on the person: 'komşudan ... istedim' is literally requested from the neighbor.

target: Ben havaalanında hiçbir şey istemedim.
english: I didn't want anything at the airport.
tip: 'hiçbir şey' (nothing) still needs a negative verb: 'hiçbir şey istemedim', both halves negative, means wanted nothing.

target: Hasan okuldan şaşkınlıkla geldi.
english: Hasan came from school in surprise.
tip: Adding -la to a noun tells how an action happens: 'şaşkınlıkla' means with surprise, from 'şaşkınlık' plus -la.

target: Komşular birbirlerine yardım ediyor.
english: The neighbors help each other.
tip: 'yardım etmek' (to help) takes the -e ending, since help goes to someone: hence 'birbirlerine', to each other, carries -e.

target: Sabahtan beri seni bekliyorum.
english: I've been waiting for you since morning.
tip: 'beri' (since) follows a noun ending in -tan/-den: 'sabahtan beri' means since morning, 'sabah' plus -tan plus 'beri'.

target: Annemin yemekleri her zaman çok lezzetli.
english: My mother's food is always very delicious.
tip: Possession marks both words: in 'annemin yemekleri' the owner takes -in and the thing owned takes -leri.

target: Üç yıl önce bu mahalleye taşındık.
english: We moved to this neighbourhood three years ago.
tip: After a length of time, 'önce' means ago: 'üç yıl önce' is three years ago.

target: Bu yemek tarifi annemden anneanneme kadar gelmiş.
english: This recipe has been passed down from my grandmother to my mother.
tip: The -mış past reports something not personally witnessed: 'gelmiş' means it has come, so the story goes, unlike plain 'geldi'.

target: Kış ayları yaz aylarından çok daha soğuk oluyor.
english: Winter months are much colder than summer months.
tip: Comparison uses -dan plus 'daha': 'yaz aylarından çok daha soğuk' means much colder than summer months.

target: Anneannem her pazar bize gelir ve yemek yapar.
english: My grandmother comes to us every Sunday and cooks.
tip: The -ir/-ar ending marks habits: 'gelir' and 'yapar' mean she regularly comes and cooks, not a one-time event.

target: Toplantımız saat üçte başlayacak.
english: Our meeting will start at three o'clock.
tip: Clock times take the -de/-te ending: 'saat üçte' means at three o'clock.

target: Yemekten sonra Türk kahvesi içtik.
english: We drank Turkish coffee after dinner.
tip: 'sonra' (after) follows a noun ending in -ten/-tan: 'yemekten sonra' means after the meal, 'yemek' plus -ten.

target: Kendine güvenmelisin, yapabilirsin.
english: You should believe in yourself, you can do it.
tip: The -meli suffix means should or must: 'güvenmelisin' = you should believe in yourself. It attaches straight onto the verb stem.

target: Zaman zaman eski arkadaşlarımla buluşurum.
english: From time to time I meet with old friends.
tip: The -la ending means with: 'arkadaşlarımla' = with my friends. It stacks after the -ım (my) part: 'arkadaş', 'lar', 'ım', 'la'.

target: Dedem her akşam radyo dinlerdi.
english: My grandfather used to listen to the radio every evening.
tip: The habit ending -r plus -di means used to: 'dinlerdi' = he used to listen. It marks a repeated past habit, not one finished action.

target: Küçük kardeşim hep benden öğrenmek ister.
english: My little sibling always wants to learn from me.
tip: The -den ending marks a source: 'benden' = from me. Learning from someone uses it, so 'öğrenmek' pairs with the -den form.

target: Yeni telefon aldım ama alışamadım henüz.
english: I bought a new phone but I haven't gotten used to it yet.
tip: The -ama inside a verb means cannot: 'alışamadım' = I couldn't get used to it. Without it, 'alışmadım' = I didn't get used to it.

target: Evde iki kedi ve bir köpek besliyoruz.
english: We keep two cats and one dog at home.
tip: After a number the noun stays singular: 'iki kedi', not 'kediler', and 'bir köpek' stays bare. The number already signals plural.

target: Bu hafta sonu dışarı çıkmayacağız, evde dinleneceğiz.
english: We won't go out this weekend, we'll rest at home.
tip: Negative future is stem plus -ma plus future -acak: 'çıkmayacağız' = we will not go out, from 'çık', 'ma', 'yacağız'.

target: Her sabah erken kalkarım ve yürüyüşe çıkarım.
english: I get up early every morning and go for a walk.
tip: The verb 'çıkmak' takes the -e form for a goal: 'yürüyüşe çıkarım' = I go out for a walk. The walk carries the -e ending.

target: Kaza çok büyükmüş, yol saatlerce kapalı kalmış.
english: The accident was apparently very serious, and the road remained closed for hours.
tip: The -mış ending marks news you infer or were told, not saw: 'kalmış' = it apparently stayed closed.
